messages.subject: compRelSEM with ordered indicator
parts:
Hi,

I'm running a 1-factor CFA with 4 indicators, one of which is an ordered variable.  Should the compRelSEM still be able to return an omega value for the fit?  It does when I don't specify the variable as ordered, or if I don't include it, but gives NA when I do.  My code is:

model <- ' y =~ a + b + c + d '
fit <- cfa(model, ordered = "c")

lavaan version: 0.6.17
semTools version: 0.5-6
R version: 4.3.2

Sorry for the very basic question!

messages.author: 94f286b5f4d86673
messages.subject: Re: compRelSEM with ordered indicator
parts:
Never mind, I see the metric can't be calculated when there is a combination of continuous and ordinal variables.
In this case is it appropriate to use the following formula for omega:
sum(lavInspect(fit,"std.lv")$lambda)^2 / ( sum(lavInspect(fit,"std.lv")$lambda)^2 + sum(lavInspect(fit,"theta")) ) ?
Or does this suffer from the issue that the covariances are based on the underlying latent continuous indicator and not the observed ordinal indicator?

I see the metric can't be calculated when there is a combination of continuous and ordinal variables.
In this case is it appropriate to use the following formula for omega:
sum(lavInspect(fit,"std.lv")$lambda)^2 / ( sum(lavInspect(fit,"std.lv")$lambda)^2 + sum(lavInspect(fit,"theta")) ) ?
Or does this suffer from the issue that the covariances are based on the underlying latent continuous indicator and not the observed ordinal indicator?

Correct.  No one has proposed formulas for the case with mixed indicators.
